question: Which quick screening tool is specifically designed to check for substance use risks in teenagers?

options.A: Braden scale
options.B: Glasgow Coma Scale
options.C: CRAFFT questionnaire
options.D: Apgar score

question: Which strategy works best when designing health messages for communities with low literacy levels?

options.A: Using pictorial guides, local radio jingles, and interactive drama performances
options.B: Relying entirely on detailed medical charts during community lectures
options.C: Distributing dense academic textbooks written in English about chronic diseases
options.D: Requiring all participants to read online health blogs before clinic visits

explanation: Wonderful! Pictures, local drama, and radio bypass reading barriers, making health education fun and easy for everyone to understand. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T15#GNS313_U3_T15_h5)

question: Why do nurses set specific alert limits (thresholds) on patient wearables?

options.A: To ensure the device battery never runs out of power unexpectedly
options.B: To stop patients from looking at their own heart rate data
options.C: To comply with government laws regarding smartphone manufacturing
options.D: To prevent alert fatigue from minor, harmless data fluctuations

explanation: Setting smart limits stops alarms from ringing over tiny movements, keeping nurses focused on actual emergencies. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h4)

question: Which of these actions does NOT help promote independence in a visually impaired patient?

options.A: Teaching them to organize clothing by texture and location
options.B: Doing all of their personal grooming tasks for them to save time
options.C: Encouraging the use of a white cane for outdoor travel
options.D: Suggesting talking clocks and large-print books

explanation: Spot on! Doing everything for them actually takes away their independence and confidence. We want to support them in doing what they can! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T13#GNS324_U4_T13_h5)

question: Which nutritional shortage is most commonly linked to tiredness and poor school performance in teenagers?

options.A: Iron deficiency anemia
options.B: Sodium overload
options.C: Excess protein intake
options.D: Vitamin C toxicity

explanation: You got it! Low iron reduces oxygen flow in the blood, leaving students feeling sluggish and finding it hard to concentrate in class. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T007#GNS227_U2_T007_h6)

question: Why must you warn a patient who just used a numbing mouthwash (like viscous lidocaine) to be careful before eating?

options.A: Lidocaine permanently destroys the taste buds on the tongue
options.B: The medication reacts badly with food and causes severe nausea
options.C: Swallowing the numbing agent stops stomach digestion completely
options.D: Numbing the mouth can lead to accidental biting or choking

explanation: When the mouth is numb, patients can easily bite their cheeks or tongue by mistake, or even choke on their food. Safety first! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T4#GNS213_U3_T4_h5)

question: Why is tracking defaulters an effective strategy for raising immunization rates?

options.A: It punishes parents who fail to pay official clinic registration fees
options.B: It reduces the total number of vaccines the clinic needs to order
options.C: It eliminates the need for any public health education campaigns
options.D: It ensures children who missed doses are identified and brought back to complete vaccination

explanation: Spot on! Following up on missed appointments prevents partial vaccination and makes sure children get full protection. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T69#GNS214_U1_T69_h8)

question: Which eye condition usually damages side vision first due to a buildup of pressure inside the eyeball?

options.A: Glaucoma
options.B: Diabetic retinopathy
options.C: Macular degeneration
options.D: Cataracts

explanation: Glaucoma happens when pressure builds up inside the eye, slowly damaging the optic nerve. It usually starts by affecting the outer or side vision first. You've got this! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T8#GNS324_U4_T8_h2)

question: How should an emotionally intelligent leader respond to a nurse dealing with burnout?

options.A: By validating their feelings and offering meaningful support
options.B: By giving them a formal warning for poor productivity
options.C: By ignoring the issue so it resolves itself over time
options.D: By assigning them extra weekend shifts to build toughness

explanation: Burnout is real. A great leader spots the exhaustion, listens with empathy, and offers genuine support instead of piling on more stress or punishment. [learn more](GST321_U3_T4#GST321_U3_T4_h4)

question: When should a sharps disposal container be safely sealed and replaced?

options.A: Only when it is completely overflowing at the top
options.B: At the very end of every calendar month
options.C: When it reaches the three-quarters full mark
options.D: As soon as the first single syringe is dropped inside

explanation: Stopping at three-quarters full prevents needles from poking out of the opening and endangering staff who handle the waste. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h5)

question: At what angle should a nurse insert the needle for a subcutaneous vaccine like measles?

options.A: At a 90-degree angle
options.B: At a 45-degree angle
options.C: At a 15-degree angle
options.D: Straight down at a 180-degree angle

explanation: Spot on! A 45-degree angle lets you place the vaccine nicely into the fatty layer just under the skin instead of going deep into the muscle. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T63#GNS214_U1_T63_h5)

question: Which part of a normal ECG tracing shows the electrical recovery of the ventricles?

options.A: QRS complex
options.B: P wave
options.C: PR interval
options.D: T wave

explanation: The T wave is like the heart taking a deep breath and resetting its electrical charge after a hard squeeze, getting ready for the next beat. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is a major emotional and social challenge that HIV-positive mums often face regarding how they feed their babies?

options.A: Complete lack of interest in infant nutritional needs
options.B: Legal restrictions against breastfeeding in public places
options.C: Inability to find pediatric clinics in rural areas
options.D: Fear of stigma and disclosure within their communities

explanation: The fear of being judged or accidentally revealing their status to family and neighbors weighs heavily on many mums. Empathy goes a long way! [learn more](GNS216_U6_T12#GNS216_U6_T12_h6)

question: What is a great way to reach people with low reading skills during a public safety campaign?

options.A: Posting complex legal notices online
options.B: Using visual aids and pictures
options.C: Relying solely on written email newsletters
options.D: Distributing dense academic textbooks

explanation: You got it! Pictures and clear demonstrations help share safety messages effectively with everyone in the community. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T10#GNS315_U5_T10_h4)

question: Why does a skin pinch test help nurses check a patient's hydration level?

options.A: Electrolyte imbalances cause immediate muscle contractions under the skin
options.B: Lack of blood flow makes the skin permanently thick and rigid
options.C: Dehydrated skin loses elasticity because interstitial fluid is depleted
options.D: Fever causes the skin cells to lock together tightly

explanation: When the fluid between skin cells dries up, the skin loses its natural stretchiness and takes longer to bounce back flat after pinching. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T18#GNS215_U6_T18_h5)

question: What nursing term describes when a harsh chemotherapy drug accidentally leaks out of the vein into the surrounding tissue?

options.A: Anaphylaxis
options.B: Extravasation
options.C: Phlebitis
options.D: Infiltration

explanation: You've got this! Extravasation happens when a vesicant drug escapes into surrounding tissues, which can cause serious local tissue damage. Always protect your IV sites! [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h4)

question: Why do nurses use continuous IV infusions for certain medications?

options.A: Elimination of all infection risks
options.B: Exact control over blood levels
options.C: Lower cost than oral tablets
options.D: Zero requirement for site monitoring

explanation: Think of a continuous infusion as a steady drip that keeps the medicine level just right in the body over time, avoiding sudden spikes or drops. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T5#GNS125_U3_T5_h2)

question: When entering an isolation room, what is the very first piece of PPE you should put on?

options.A: N95 respirator
options.B: Isolation gown
options.C: Eye goggles
options.D: Sterile gloves

explanation: Great job! Think of it from the body up: you put your gown on first to cover your uniform completely before touching masks or gloves. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h4)

question: Why should researchers be honest about study limitations in their published papers?

options.A: To trick reviewers into approving weak methodologies
options.B: To avoid paying taxes on research grants
options.C: To make the paper shorter and easier to read
options.D: To ensure readers interpret findings with appropriate caution

explanation: You nailed it! Total honesty about what a study *couldn't* do stops clinicians from misapplying the results on the wards. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T2#GNS217_U2_T2_h7)

question: What is the main advantage of using a second messenger system like cAMP?

options.A: It stops the target cell from responding too quickly
options.B: It prevents hormones from ever leaving the bloodstream
options.C: It greatly amplifies the initial hormonal signal
options.D: It allows the hormone to physically enter the nucleus

explanation: A single hormone molecule binding outside can trigger the production of many second messengers, multiplying the cell's response. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T9#GNS211_U1_T9_h3)

question: Why should you pre-test your IEC materials with a small group before mass printing them?

options.A: To sell the materials to community members to raise funds for the clinic
options.B: To ensure the messages are clear and culturally appropriate before full release
options.C: To satisfy government paperwork requirements without involving the community
options.D: To test the physical strength and durability of the printing paper

explanation: Pre-testing helps you catch confusing words or awkward pictures early, saving you from wasting time and money on materials that won't work. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T5#GNS124_U5_T5_h7)

question: Why do we use an intersectoral team approach in health care?

options.A: To combine different sectors to address the root causes of poor health
options.B: To train doctors to perform duties traditionally handled by agricultural workers
options.C: To increase the cost of running primary health care centers
options.D: To merge all community clinics into a single administrative unit

explanation: Great job! Health isn't just about medicine—it depends on social, economic, and environmental factors. Bringing different fields together helps us tackle these big issues at their core. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h1)

question: What is a major long-term risk for someone staying on an extremely strict low-fat diet for months?

options.A: Sudden increase in digestive enzyme output
options.B: Permanent enlargement of the stomach
options.C: Deficiencies in fat-soluble vitamins
options.D: Excessive accumulation of muscle mass

explanation: Without a little healthy dietary fat over time, the body struggles to absorb key vitamins like A, D, E, and K. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T005#GNS227_U6_T005_h8)

question: A survivor of FGM shows signs of severe anxiety during a routine gynecological checkup. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Leave the room and document that the patient refused all care
options.B: Stop the examination, reassure the patient, and proceed only with her consent
options.C: Administer a strong sedative immediately without discussing it with her
options.D: Firmly insist the patient stay still so the doctor can finish quickly

explanation: Respecting the patient's boundaries and restoring her sense of control is essential for survivors experiencing anxiety. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h6)

question: A health agency stops giving blind budgets to hospitals and instead pays them based on actual quality services delivered. What is this called?

options.A: Donor dependency
options.B: Risk fragmentation
options.C: Strategic purchasing
options.D: Out-of-pocket spending

explanation: Strategic purchasing is like smart shopping—instead of throwing money blindly at a hospital, the agency pays wisely for specific, quality care to get the best health outcomes. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h3)

question: What is the main difference between a spontaneous abortion and an induced abortion?

options.A: Induced abortions happen completely by accident
options.B: Induced abortions are always caused by chromosomal defects
options.C: Spontaneous abortions only occur during the third trimester
options.D: Spontaneous abortions happen naturally without outside intervention

explanation: A spontaneous abortion (miscarriage) happens on its own due to natural factors, while an induced abortion is brought on by intentional medical or surgical steps. Simple and clear! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T005#GNS226_U5_T005_h1)

question: What happens during tubular reabsorption in the nephron?

options.A: Urine is pushed down the ureters through muscular contractions
options.B: Extra metabolic wastes are pumped from the blood into the tubule
options.C: Useful substances are moved from the renal tubules back into the blood
options.D: Blood pressure forces large proteins through the glomerular membrane

explanation: Your kidneys filter a lot of good stuff by accident at first! Tubular reabsorption acts like a salvage yard, pulling water, sugar, and nutrients back into your bloodstream. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T1#GNS213_U4_T1_h4)

question: Why does milk make it so easy for bacteria to grow quickly?

options.A: It is usually stored in open containers in the market
options.B: It undergoes heavy chemical processing before packaging
options.C: It contains a high concentration of essential nutrients
options.D: It is naturally warm and has a very low pH level

explanation: Spot on! Milk is packed with proteins, fats, and sugars, which makes it a rich food source for microorganisms to feed and multiply on. [learn more](GST114_U5_T5#GST114_U5_T5_h1)

question: Which complication is closely linked to rapid weight loss from severe calorie restriction?

options.A: Permanent kidney failure
options.B: Enlarged heart valves
options.C: High red blood cell count
options.D: Gallstone formation

explanation: Spot on! Losing weight too fast causes the liver to release extra cholesterol into bile, which can easily form gallstones in the gallbladder. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T010#GNS227_U6_T010_h5)

question: Why are involuntary reflexes like coughing and vomiting important for survival?

options.A: They increase the amount of red blood cells in circulation
options.B: They cool down the body during a high fever
options.C: They protect the body from harmful substances and blockages
options.D: They help the digestive system absorb extra vitamins

explanation: These protective reflexes quickly expel irritants or foreign items from the airway and digestive tract to prevent injury. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h5)

question: What makes farming pesticides particularly dangerous in rural areas?

options.A: Farmers use them exclusively as food flavoring agents in local dishes
options.B: They are frequently stored near food items and handled without protective gear
options.C: They only affect animals and have zero toxic impact on human physiology
options.D: They lose their toxicity completely within a few minutes of application

explanation: Spot on! When chemicals are kept close to food and used without gloves or masks, accidental poisoning happens easily. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T13#GNS313_U3_T13_h2)

question: What makes paediatric nutrition different from adult nutrition?

options.A: Reducing total daily caloric intake
options.B: Preventing lifestyle diseases like hypertension
options.C: Supporting rapid growth and organ maturation
options.D: Maintaining a stable body weight over time

explanation: You've got this! Children grow fast and their organs are still developing, so they need special nutrients. Adults, on the other hand, mostly just need to maintain their weight. Keep up the great work! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T012#GNS227_U7_T012_h1)

question: A junior nurse is told to do a dressing change a certain way simply because 'that is how we've always done it here.' What type of inquiry is this?

options.A: Traditional and authority-based inquiry
options.B: Randomized controlled testing
options.C: Empirical scientific inquiry
options.D: Systematic qualitative inquiry

explanation: Relying on past custom and instructions from senior staff without checking the literature is traditional and authority-based inquiry. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T2#GNS217_U1_T2_h3)

question: A maternity nurse ignores a fetal monitor beep because too many false alarms sounded earlier. What is this called?

options.A: Fixation error
options.B: Memory lapse
options.C: Confirmation bias
options.D: Alert fatigue

explanation: Well done! When machines beep too often for nothing, we get 'alert fatigue' and might sadly miss the one time the alarm is actually saving a life. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T7#GNS312_U5_T7_h2)

question: How can chronic (long-term) inflammation lead to a cervical polyp?

options.A: It destroys local nerve endings
options.B: It directly causes malignant cell transformation
options.C: It triggers abnormal tissue proliferation over time
options.D: It blocks the production of estrogen

explanation: Think of it like skin getting a callus from constant friction. Ongoing irritation makes the cervical tissue grow extra cells, forming a polyp over time. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h2)

question: Which instrument is best for capturing deep, personal stories from patients about chronic illness?

options.A: Interview guide
options.B: Simple questionnaire
options.C: Blood pressure cuff
options.D: Checklist of bedside actions

explanation: Interview guides allow researchers to ask open-ended questions and explore personal experiences in detail. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T21#GNS224_U1_T21_h3)

question: How do modern apology laws treat expressions of sympathy from healthcare providers?

options.A: They remove all licensing requirements for doctors involved in adverse events
options.B: They force the hospital to pay double compensation in every civil lawsuit
options.C: They protect humanitarian expressions of sorrow from being used as evidence of fault
options.D: They make it illegal for any nurse to speak directly to a patient's family

explanation: Apology protection laws encourage honesty by making sure that showing human empathy and sorrow cannot be used in court as proof of guilt. [learn more](GST319_U6_T3#GST319_U6_T3_h5)

question: Which home care instruction is most critical for a patient who just had a liver biopsy?

options.A: Call the clinic or return if you feel severe shoulder or belly pain
options.B: Go for long daily jogs to boost blood circulation
options.C: Scrub the tiny wound hard with soap immediately
options.D: Take aspirin every morning to prevent clots

explanation: You got it! Severe pain can be an early warning sign of internal bleeding or other complications, so patients must report it right away. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T10#GNS221_U2_T10_h7)

question: What is the main difference between measurement and evaluation in nursing school?

options.A: Measurement is done by students, while evaluation is done strictly by hospital managers.
options.B: Measurement assigns numbers, while evaluation interprets those numbers to make a judgment.
options.C: Measurement evaluates clinical skills, while evaluation tests written knowledge.
options.D: Measurement focuses on attitudes, while evaluation focuses purely on psychomotor tasks.

explanation: Think of measurement as gathering raw data like your test score (e.g., 75%), while evaluation decides what that score actually means for your progress as a nurse. You've got this! [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h1)

question: When is a statistical table best used in a research report?

options.A: When replacing the narrative text entirely
options.B: When describing a single patient's emotional journey
options.C: When presenting large amounts of precise numerical data
options.D: When showing general trends and patterns over time

explanation: Tables excel at organizing large volumes of exact numbers so readers can easily locate specific values. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T4#GNS224_U2_T4_h2)

question: In Nigeria's routine immunization schedule, which vaccines are given right at birth?

options.A: Measles 1, Yellow Fever, and Meningitis
options.B: Pentavalent 1, PCV 1, and Rotavirus 1
options.C: BCG, OPV 0, and Hepatitis B birth dose
options.D: Inactivated Polio Vaccine and Tetanus toxoid

explanation: Always remember the birth trio: BCG, oral polio zero (OPV 0), and the Hepatitis B birth dose are given before the baby leaves the maternity ward! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T16#GNS215_U6_T16_h4)

question: What is the correct hand motion on the push rims when a patient is moving a manual wheelchair forward?

options.A: Grip at ten o'clock and push forward down to two o'clock

options.C: Smack the spokes of the wheels with an open palm
options.D: Hold the hand rims tightly still while kicking the floor

question: Which of these is NOT a common financial or social barrier to healthcare access in Nigeria?

options.A: High out-of-pocket expenses for routine medications and blood tests
options.B: Financial strain caused by the loss of daily income during hospital admissions
options.C: Free and unlimited universal healthcare coverage for all citizens
options.D: Long travel distances from rural villages to tertiary teaching hospitals

explanation: If only! Sadly, free universal healthcare isn't the reality yet, meaning out-of-pocket costs remain a huge hurdle for many patients. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T4#GNS311_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is the medical term for excessive thirst experienced by a client with high blood sugar?

options.A: Proteinuria
options.B: Polyuria
options.C: Polyphagia
options.D: Polydipsia

explanation: Polydipsia is the medical word for extreme thirst, which happens because the body loses a lot of water through frequent urination. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T8#GNS222_U2_T8_h4)

question: Why do home health nurses need strong independent clinical judgment?

options.A: They make all hospital admission policies
options.B: They are required to perform major surgeries at home
options.C: They do not need to follow any medical protocols
options.D: They often work alone without immediate peer support

explanation: When you're out on a home visit solo, you have to trust your own assessment skills and critical thinking until you can consult your team. You're building these exact skills right now! [learn more](GNS324_U2_T7#GNS324_U2_T7_h4)

question: Why is it important to let a hot sterilized pack cool down inside the autoclave before touching it?

options.A: Hot metal instruments will bend out of shape if exposed to room air
options.B: The packaging material will immediately catch fire if moved too quickly
options.C: Cooling down resets the chemical indicator strip color back to normal
options.D: Touching it while hot can draw moisture through the wrapper and contaminate the contents

explanation: Touching a hot, damp pack creates condensation. Water droplets act like an elevator for bacteria, letting them slip right through the wrapper! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h7)

question: Why is diet therapy such an important part of your daily nursing duties?

options.A: Nurses must personally cook all meals served in the hospital ward
options.B: Nurses are responsible for monitoring patient tolerance and supporting the prescribed nutrition plan
options.C: Dietary plans replace the need for physical assessments
options.D: Doctors never check what patients are eating

explanation: Since you spend the most time with patients, you are in the best position to see if they are enjoying their food and how well their body is handling it! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h1)

question: Which of the following is a core part of primary health care delivery in an IDP camp?

options.A: Managing large-scale commercial agricultural farms
options.B: Performing complex open-heart surgical procedures daily
options.C: Providing essential routine immunizations and basic medicines
options.D: Issuing international travel passports to camp residents

explanation: Primary health care is all about everyday essentials like vaccines, basic treatments, and keeping the community healthy. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T20#GNS225_U5_T20_h4)

question: Which of the following is an example of secondary data in a community assessment?

options.A: Direct observation of stagnant water behind residential houses
options.B: A brand new questionnaire filled out by household heads today
options.C: Interviews conducted by the nurse with mothers in the market
options.D: Past clinic attendance registers and local census reports

explanation: Secondary data refers to information that has already been collected and recorded by someone else for other purposes. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h5)

question: During a pediatric resuscitation, how often should epinephrine be given?

options.A: Only after five defibrillation shocks
options.B: Every 3 to 5 minutes
options.C: Once every hour
options.D: Every 30 seconds

explanation: Epinephrine is a trusty emergency medication given every 3 to 5 minutes during a code to help keep blood flowing to the heart and brain. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T3#GNS212_U2_T3_h7)

question: In the PDSA cycle, during which phase does the nurse actually carry out the proposed change on a small scale?

options.A: Act phase
options.B: Plan phase
options.C: Study phase
options.D: Do phase

explanation: Keep it up! The 'Do' phase is where you roll up your sleeves and try out the new idea on a small scale to see how it feels in practice. [learn more](GST319_U2_T1#GST319_U2_T1_h4)

question: Why is keeping a hospital ward calm and clean during mealtime so important?

options.A: It prevents nurses from having to clean bedsheets
options.B: It speeds up the digestion rate in the stomach
options.C: It stops patients from talking to one another
options.D: It encourages better appetite and food consumption

explanation: Spot on! A peaceful, clean, and pleasant dining vibe lowers stress and makes patients actually want to eat their meals. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T002#GNS227_U2_T002_h8)

question: What does 'confabulation' mean when caring for a patient with Korsakoff syndrome?

options.A: Making up stories to fill memory gaps without intent to lie
options.B: Refusing to speak to anyone about personal history
options.C: Deliberately deceiving healthcare workers about past events
options.D: Experiencing vivid visual hallucinations during the night

explanation: Don't worry, they aren't trying to trick you! Confabulation is when a patient unconsciously fills in memory blanks with made-up details, and they genuinely believe it happened. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T8#GNS222_U4_T8_h1)

question: How many natural narrow spots (constrictions) does a normal human ureter have?

options.A: Three
options.B: One
options.C: Two
options.D: Five

explanation: Spot on! There are three tight spots along the way where stubborn kidney stones love to get stuck. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T2#GNS121_U2_T2_h2)

question: Which of the following is an environmental hazard that increases fall risk in older adults?

options.A: Bright, glare-free overhead lighting
options.B: Loose throw rugs on the floor
options.C: Properly fitted rubber-soled shoes
options.D: Sturdy handrails along the hallway

explanation: Unsecured rugs frequently catch on shoes or mobility devices, causing accidental trips and falls. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T24#GNS222_U1_T24_h5)

question: Why is relying on informal personal shortcuts instead of established hospital policy dangerous?

options.A: It forces the hospital to buy expensive new computer systems
options.B: It creates inconsistency and increases the risk of medical errors
options.C: It automatically increases the nurse's monthly salary
options.D: It saves too much time and makes nursing look too easy

explanation: Informal shortcuts bypass vital safety checks, leading to unpredictable care quality and a higher chance of making a mistake. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h7)

question: What does indirect calorimetry measure to figure out a patient's energy use?

options.A: Total body fat percentage using electrical currents
options.B: Blood glucose levels over a twenty-four hour period
options.C: Oxygen consumption and carbon dioxide production
options.D: Internal core body temperature via skin sensors

explanation: By checking the air a patient breathes in and out, this clever test calculates exactly how much energy their cells are burning. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T014#GNS227_U1_T014_h5)

question: What is another common name for cancellous bone?

options.A: Cortical bone
options.B: Compact bone
options.C: Spongy bone
options.D: Dense bone

explanation: You got this! Cancellous bone is often called spongy bone because if you look at it inside, it has a porous, honeycomb-like pattern just like a kitchen sponge. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T3#GNS121_U3_T3_h1)

question: How do adult day care homes primarily benefit family caregivers?

options.A: By taking over complete legal and financial responsibility for the client
options.B: By training family members to become licensed practical nurses
options.C: By permanently removing the need for any home-based care
options.D: By offering temporary respite to prevent physical and emotional burnout

explanation: These facilities give family caregivers a necessary break from constant responsibilities, helping them sustain their own health and continue working or managing personal tasks. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h1)

question: Maternal education in Nigeria is most closely linked to which of these health outcomes?

options.A: Cost of private health insurance
options.B: Frequency of major surgical operations
options.C: Availability of hospital bed spaces
options.D: Child immunization and nutrition rates

explanation: Correct! Educated mothers are generally better positioned to access preventive child healthcare and practice good infant nutrition. [learn more](GST322_U3_T4#GST322_U3_T4_h4)

question: A community health nurse wants to build strong herd immunity against a viral illness in a local village. What should be the top priority?

options.A: Distributing vitamin supplements
options.B: Isolating all healthy children indoors
options.C: Testing local water supplies for bacteria
options.D: Mass vaccination campaigns

explanation: Brilliant! Mass vaccination builds a protective shield around the whole community, making it almost impossible for the virus to find a new victim. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T2#GNS313_U1_T2_h7)

question: Why is prompt transportation of a biological specimen to the laboratory important?

options.A: To reduce the cost of electricity in the clinic
options.B: To ensure the requisition form does not get lost
options.C: To prevent sample degradation or bacterial overgrowth
options.D: To make sure the laboratory staff stay busy

explanation: Leaving samples sitting out too long ruins cells and allows bacteria to multiply, leading to false test results. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T4#GNS124_U6_T4_h5)

question: A community health nurse wants to reach residents who never visit the clinic. What is the best first step?

options.A: Conduct house-to-house surveys and community profiling
options.B: Report the entire community to the federal ministry of health
options.C: Wait patiently in the clinic office for someone to ask for help
options.D: Close the primary health center and move to a big city

explanation: Sometimes patients can't or won't come to the clinic. Going out to meet them through home visits and community mapping is the best way to find those who need help the most. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T7#GNS124_U6_T7_h2)

question: Which germ is the main cause of tuberculosis (TB)?

options.A: Streptococcus pneumoniae
options.B: Mycobacterium tuberculosis
options.C: Corynebacterium diphtheriae
options.D: Bordetella pertussis

explanation: TB is caused by a bacterium called Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It loves to settle in the lungs! You'll get this easily with practice. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T18#GNS324_U4_T18_h1)

question: Why is a patient told not to eat or drink (NPO) before a laparoscopy?

options.A: To prevent the surgical instruments from getting dirty
options.B: To ensure the patient loses weight before surgery
options.C: To stop the kidneys from producing urine
options.D: To reduce the risk of aspiration during anesthesia

explanation: Spot on! Keeping the stomach empty stops food or vomit from flowing up and entering the lungs while the patient is fast asleep under anesthesia. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h4)

question: What happens to complement protein levels (such as C3 and C4) in the blood during active serum sickness?

options.A: They decrease
options.B: They disappear entirely
options.C: They remain completely normal
options.D: They increase

explanation: Think of complement proteins as fuel used up in a fire; because the immune reaction is working overtime, these levels drop in the blood. [learn more](GST114_U4_T10#GST114_U4_T10_h5)

question: How does SIMV (Synchronized Intermittent Mandatory Ventilation) differ from Assist-Control mode?

options.A: SIMV delivers breaths only when the patient makes zero respiratory effort
options.B: SIMV allows spontaneous breaths between mandatory machine breaths without extra volume support
options.C: SIMV is only used for patients who are paralyzed or heavily sedated
options.D: SIMV completely controls every single breath the patient takes without exception

explanation: SIMV gives the patient a bit of freedom! The machine gives scheduled breaths, but in between those, the patient can take their own natural breaths without the machine forcing extra air. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T6#GNS315_U3_T6_h2)

question: Where does personal protective equipment rank in the hierarchy of hazard controls?

options.A: Below administrative controls but above substitution
options.B: At the very bottom as a last resort
options.C: At the very top as the best choice
options.D: Right above elimination

explanation: PPE is the last line of defense because it does not stop the hazard itself, only protects the individual wearing it if other controls fail. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h6)

question: What term describes the thinning of the cervix during the first stage of labor?

options.A: Engagement
options.B: Effacement
options.C: Extension
options.D: Descent

explanation: Cervical effacement refers to the shortening and thinning of the cervical canal before and during the dilation process. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h2)

question: What important detail must be included when documenting an intradermal injection?

options.A: Brand name of the alcohol swab
options.B: Name of the nurse's supervisor
options.C: Patient's favorite arm preference
options.D: Exact anatomical site used

explanation: Recording the exact location is necessary so the healthcare team can find the correct spot when returning to read the test results. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h7)

question: What is another common name for prenatal care?

options.A: Neonatal monitoring
options.B: Postpartum care
options.C: Gynecological screening
options.D: Antenatal care

explanation: Prenatal care is widely referred to as antenatal care, representing health services provided during the period of pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h1)

question: How do open refuse dumps contribute to foodborne illnesses in a community?

options.A: They cause the air temperature in the kitchen to rise too high
options.B: They attract pests like flies and rodents that transfer pathogens to food
options.C: They increase the mineral content of nearby groundwater supplies
options.D: They remove all helpful bacteria from the local environment

explanation: You got it! Pests love open garbage; flies and rats feed on the dirt and then march right over uncovers food, leaving dangerous germs behind. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T21#GNS214_U1_T21_h5)

question: What does the acronym IEC stand for in public health?

options.A: Investigation, Environment, and Community
options.B: Immunization, Education, and Care
options.C: Information, Education, and Communication
options.D: Infection, Evaluation, and Control

explanation: IEC is a core public health strategy that stands for Information, Education, and Communication, used to guide community health promotion. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h1)

question: A researcher spots a few strange blood pressure numbers that look like typos in the database. What is the best first step?

options.A: Ignore the mistakes and run the statistical analysis anyway
options.B: Change the numbers randomly to fit the average reading
options.C: Check the original paper records to verify the correct entry
options.D: Delete all the patient records so they do not ruin the study

explanation: Data cleaning means checking suspicious entries against original source documents rather than guessing or deleting data carelessly. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T3#GNS224_U2_T3_h2)

question: Why is just smelling food a poor way to tell if it is safe to eat?

options.A: Sniffing food exposes your lungs to dangerous kitchen fumes.
options.B: Harmful food poisoning bacteria often do not change how food smells or looks.
options.C: Spoiled food always smells sweet instead of sour.
options.D: Human noses cannot detect any bad odors coming from spoiled meat.

explanation: Dangerous germs can hide in food without changing its scent or look at all. Always check expiry dates and store food safely! [learn more](GNS227_U3_T012#GNS227_U3_T012_h8)

question: What term is used to measure the amount of tracer absorbed in a specific spot on a PET scan?

options.A: Systemic Urine Volume
options.B: Standardized Uptake Value
options.C: Specific Ultrasound Velocity
options.D: Serum Utilization Variable

explanation: You got it! Radiologists use the Standardized Uptake Value (SUV) as a handy number to measure just how much tracer activity is happening in a specific tissue. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T14#GNS123_U2_T14_h7)

question: What sensation should you warn a patient to expect when the barium liquid goes in?

options.A: Total numbness from the waist down to the toes
options.B: Heavy sleepiness and deep drowsiness
options.C: A sharp burning feeling across the skin of the belly
options.D: A strong urge to use the toilet and mild belly cramps

explanation: Filling the large intestine with fluid naturally creates pressure and triggers bowel contractions. Giving patients a heads-up helps ease their anxiety. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T9#GNS212_U1_T9_h4)

question: If a patient's potassium levels go haywire, which body system is in the most immediate danger?

options.A: Cardiovascular system
options.B: Integumentary system
options.C: Digestive system
options.D: Respiratory system

explanation: Spot on! Potassium is like the electrical spark plug for the heart. When it's unbalanced, the heart's rhythm is the first thing we worry about. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T11#GNS121_U2_T11_h2)

question: What happens during the process of clot retraction?

options.A: White blood cells destroy excess fibrinogen in the plasma
options.B: Platelets contract to pull the edges of the broken vessel together
options.C: The blood pressure drops to prevent further vessel damage
options.D: Red blood cells multiply to replace the lost fluid volume

explanation: Clot retraction tightens the meshwork and draws the wound edges closer, which makes tissue repair much easier. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h5)

question: How do support groups primarily help members overcome internalized stigma?

options.A: By providing legal documents to sue community members who spread gossip
options.B: By connecting them with thriving peers who challenge false beliefs through shared experiences
options.C: By hiding the medical diagnosis from all family and healthcare providers
options.D: By relocating patients to secret towns where nobody knows about the virus

explanation: Seeing healthy, confident peers living openly breaks down the false idea that the diagnosis destroys a person's worth. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T7#GNS216_U6_T7_h4)

question: When is it safe to have unprotected sex using the basal body temperature method without risking pregnancy?

options.A: Throughout the entire first week of the menstrual cycle
options.B: During the morning when the temperature spike is first noticed
options.C: On the exact day the temperature drops to its lowest point
options.D: After the temperature has remained elevated for three consecutive mornings

explanation: Three days of higher temperatures confirm that ovulation has already happened and the egg is gone. Safe zone unlocked! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T010#GNS226_U6_T010_h2)

question: A patient has an autoimmune condition where their insulin-making cells are destroyed. What lab finding is most likely?

options.A: Dangerously low blood sugar caused by excess hormone release
options.B: Rapid weight gain due to slowed metabolic breakdown
options.C: Elevated blood glucose levels due to a lack of insulin
options.D: Increased water retention and high blood pressure

explanation: Without insulin (hyposecretion), glucose can't easily enter the body's cells to be used for energy. Instead, it builds up in the bloodstream, leading to high blood sugar. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T3#GNS211_U1_T3_h8)

question: During early development, which main germ layer gives rise to all of our muscle tissues?

options.A: Blastoderm
options.B: Mesoderm
options.C: Ectoderm
options.D: Endoderm

explanation: You've got this! The middle germ layer, the mesoderm, is responsible for building our skeletal, smooth, and cardiac muscles. Think 'M for middle and muscle!' [learn more](GNS121_U3_T8#GNS121_U3_T8_h1)

question: What is the best immediate physical step to help reduce swelling right after a fresh injury?

options.A: Using a heating pad
options.B: Applying a cold pack
options.C: Placing a warm moist towel
options.D: Giving a deep tissue massage

explanation: Great clinical instinct! Cold constricts blood vessels, which slows down fluid pooling into the area and helps numb the sharp pain right away. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T7#GNS221_U3_T7_h6)

question: When you spin a blood sample in a centrifuge, what components make up that thin middle layer called the buffy coat?

options.A: White blood cells and platelets
options.B: Water and dissolved glucose
options.C: Red blood cells and hemoglobin
options.D: Albumin and clotting proteins

explanation: Well done! The buffy coat is that tiny, whitish layer sitting between the clear plasma on top and the heavy red blood cells at the bottom. It holds your infection-fighters (white blood cells) and clotting helpers (platelets). [learn more](GNS111_U2_T1#GNS111_U2_T1_h2)

question: A patient has an issue with making and circulating cerebrospinal fluid in the brain. Which cells are directly involved?

options.A: Satellite cells
options.B: Astrocytes
options.C: Ependymal cells
options.D: Schwann cells

explanation: Ependymal cells line the brain's ventricles and use tiny hair-like cilia to help produce and keep cerebrospinal fluid flowing smoothly. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T6#GNS211_U3_T6_h4)

question: Which two body systems share the use of the male urethra?

options.A: Digestive and urinary
options.B: Urinary and reproductive
options.C: Lymphatic and circulatory
options.D: Respiratory and endocrine

explanation: The male urethra pulls double duty! It acts as a passageway for passing urine from the bladder and for expelling semen. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T2#GNS121_U4_T2_h7)

question: Why is community diagnosis performed during mobilisation?

options.A: To test every resident for rare genetic disorders
options.B: To collect money from villagers for the clinic roof
options.C: To identify major local health problems and priorities together
options.D: To decide which nurses will be transferred

explanation: Community diagnosis helps health workers and residents discover what health issues matter most to the locals. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of incinerating pathological and infectious waste?

options.A: To turn biohazard waste into safe fertilizer for crops
options.B: To recover valuable metals like gold and silver
options.C: To reduce waste volume and destroy pathogens completely
options.D: To generate electricity for the hospital laundry

explanation: High-temperature burning shrinks the physical bulk of the waste while destroying all harmful germs and biological structures. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h7)

question: What is the main role of the pharmacist on a QA committee?

options.A: Managing the hospital kitchen and catering services
options.B: Monitoring medication errors and drug safety issues
options.C: Repairing broken hospital plumbing
options.D: Scheduling nurses for night and weekend shifts

explanation: You nailed it! Pharmacists bring expert knowledge on drugs, helping keep medication administration safe for every patient. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h2)

question: How do cultural traditions and religious beliefs affect a family's emotional well-being?

options.A: They guide how the family expresses feelings, handles grief, and looks for help
options.B: They decide what exact medical diagnosis a patient gets
options.C: They completely remove all mental stress
options.D: They stop caregivers from ever feeling tired or burnt out

explanation: Culture and faith are like a lens. They shape how families make sense of sickness, mourn their losses, and decide where to turn for comfort. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T6#GNS314_U1_T6_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a method of environmental vector control?

options.A: Spraying heavy doses of chemical aerosols inside every home
options.B: Clearing stagnant water pools around residential areas
options.C: Cutting away overgrown bushes near houses
options.D: Improving local waste disposal systems

explanation: Spraying chemicals is 'chemical control,' whereas cleaning up bushes, trash, and water pools is 'environmental control' because you're changing their natural habitat. [learn more](GST114_U6_T1#GST114_U6_T1_h6)

question: What happens when a healthcare market reaches 'equilibrium'?

options.A: Healthcare services become completely free of charge
options.B: The supply of doctors far exceeds patient demand
options.C: Quantity demanded equals quantity supplied
options.D: Hospital bed shortages disappear permanently everywhere

explanation: Perfect! Equilibrium just means a sweet balance: the amount of care people want matches what the health system is able to give. [learn more](GST322_U1_T2#GST322_U1_T2_h6)

question: Why does dangerously high pressure inside the skull cause changes in how a patient's pupils react?

options.A: It destroys the retina directly inside the eyeball
options.B: It compresses cranial nerve III against surrounding structures
options.C: It blocks light from entering the cornea
options.D: It stops blood flow to the tear ducts

explanation: When pressure builds up in the head, it pushes brain tissue down and squeezes Cranial Nerve III (the oculomotor nerve), which normally controls pupil size. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T20#GNS222_U3_T20_h7)

question: How can untreated illness anxiety disorder negatively affect a patient's finances?

options.A: Through repeated unnecessary medical consultations and diagnostic tests
options.B: By forcing the patient to buy expensive athletic equipment daily
options.C: Through heavy fines imposed by public health departments
options.D: By requiring mandatory long-term stays in luxury hospitals

explanation: Constant 'doctor shopping' and endless medical scans add up fast, leading to massive medical bills and financial stress over time. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T8#GNS314_U2_T8_h8)

question: What is a very common early emotional reaction after someone suddenly acquires a physical disability?

options.A: Complete indifference to their physical status
options.B: A grief response including denial and anger
options.C: Excitement about starting vocational training
options.D: Immediate acceptance and joyful adaptation

explanation: Losing body function is a heavy life blow. Feelings like shock, anger, and denial are completely normal parts of processing grief—be patient with your patients! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T17#GNS225_U5_T17_h6)

question: How does a home care nurse primarily evaluate adequate hydration and feeding in a newborn?

options.A: Checking the flexibility of the baby's finger joints
options.B: Weighing the baby before and after every single nursing session
options.C: Counting the number of wet and soiled diapers per day
options.D: Measuring the exact length of the infant every morning

explanation: Tracking wet diapers is a reliable, non-invasive way to ensure the newborn is receiving enough milk and staying hydrated. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T13#GNS324_U3_T13_h4)

question: Which of these instructions is WRONG for a patient going home with a catheter?

options.A: Wash your hands thoroughly before touching the tubing or drainage bag
options.B: Secure the catheter tubing to your thigh to prevent pulling
options.C: Keep the drainage bag higher than the level of your bladder at all times
options.D: Drink plenty of fluids throughout the day unless restricted

explanation: The bag must ALWAYS stay below the bladder! If it's higher, gravity will make the urine flow right back inside the patient. Great catch! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T16#GNS212_U1_T16_h7)

question: You are about to use a sterile pack, but you are not completely sure if the seal was broken. What should you do?

options.A: Assume it is contaminated and discard or re-sterilize it
options.B: Check if the expiration date on the package is still valid
options.C: Use it only for non-invasive bedside procedures
options.D: Wipe it down with alcohol and proceed with the task

explanation: When in doubt, throw it out! In sterile technique, any uncertainty means the item is no longer safe to use. Better safe than sorry! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h1)

question: What do we call a rehab goal that tries to stop side effects before they even happen?

options.A: Preventative goal
options.B: Supportive goal
options.C: Palliative goal
options.D: Restorative goal

explanation: Think of this as stopping trouble before it starts. Preventative rehab jumps in early to block expected physical losses. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T11#GNS321_U1_T11_h2)

question: How does the pancreas manage to do both exocrine and endocrine jobs?

options.A: It produces bile in the liver and stores it inside the gallbladder
options.B: It secretes digestive enzymes into ducts and hormones directly into blood
options.C: It chews food in the mouth and absorbs nutrients in the large intestine
options.D: It filters toxins from the blood and releases waste through the urine

explanation: The pancreas wears two hats! Through tiny tubes (ducts), it sends out digestive juices (exocrine), and straight into the bloodstream, it sends out hormones like insulin (endocrine). [learn more](GNS121_U1_T5#GNS121_U1_T5_h5)

question: What do we call the difference between what was planned in a budget and what actually happened?

options.A: Financial variance
options.B: Cash flow deficit
options.C: Capital depreciation
options.D: Asset liquidation

explanation: Variance is simply the gap or difference between your budget estimate and the reality of what you actually spent or earned. [learn more](GST321_U1_T24#GST321_U1_T24_h5)

question: Which group is often most vulnerable during a disaster due to reliance on continuous care or medical equipment?

options.A: Office workers
options.B: The elderly
options.C: Store owners
options.D: Young adults

explanation: Correct! Older adults often have chronic health needs and rely heavily on steady electricity and support that can fail during a crisis. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T10#GNS315_U5_T10_h3)

question: What is the main job of the epididymis in the male reproductive system?

options.A: Storage and maturation of sperm
options.B: Production of testosterone
options.C: Secretion of thick mucus
options.D: Filtration of blood waste

explanation: You've got this! Sperm are made in the testes, but they hang out in the epididymis to grow up and learn how to swim properly before they are released. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T5#GNS121_U4_T5_h1)

question: What is a major reason people in Nigeria often delay going to modern hospitals?

options.A: An excess of free hospitals in every rural village
options.B: Mandatory international health insurance for all citizens
options.C: The complete absence of any traditional healing practices
options.D: Financial constraints and out-of-pocket health spending

explanation: True. Having to pay out-of-pocket without easy health insurance often makes folks wait until an illness gets really bad before seeking care. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T3#GNS112_U2_T3_h7)

question: Immediately after a natural disaster, what is a top health priority for teams like the WHO?

options.A: Issuing passports to displaced citizens
options.B: Managing international commercial trade agreements
options.C: Designing long-term economic policies for the affected country
options.D: Preventing secondary health crises like waterborne disease outbreaks

explanation: Well done! When clean water systems break down, diseases like cholera can spread fast, so stopping secondary outbreaks is a top priority. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T10#GNS315_U1_T10_h3)

question: What does a p-value of less than 0.05 generally tell us in a research study?

options.A: The results are statistically significant and unlikely to be a fluke
options.B: The researchers made a major calculation error in their software
options.C: The study had five percent more patients drop out than expected
options.D: The treatment plan worked for exactly five percent of the patients

explanation: A p-value below 0.05 shows strong evidence that the result didn't just happen by pure coincidence! [learn more](GNS224_U2_T3#GNS224_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why is it so important for hospitals to ask nurses for their opinion when buying new software?

options.A: Hospital administrators are not allowed to buy software without nursing financial approval
options.B: Nurses are legally required to purchase the hardware equipment for the hospital
options.C: Nurses understand the practical bedside workflow and can spot usability issues that affect safety
options.D: Nurses are the only staff members permitted to touch computers in the building

explanation: You nailed it! Because nurses know how care actually flows at the bedside, their input ensures new technology helps rather than gets in the way. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h6)

question: How do patients with illness anxiety disorder usually react to normal, everyday body sensations like a slight muscle twitch?

options.A: They report them exclusively to family members only
options.B: They ignore them completely as routine physiology
options.C: They misinterpret them as signs of catastrophic disease
options.D: They use them to plan healthy physical exercise routines

explanation: Think of it this way: a normal minor ache gets blown completely out of proportion, making the patient convinced it's a hidden, dangerous sickness. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T8#GNS314_U2_T8_h1)

question: A mum in labour is very frightened and tense, and her labour is slowing down even though her contractions are strong. Which of the Four Ps is playing a role here?

options.A: Psyche
options.B: Passage
options.C: Passenger
options.D: Power

explanation: Fear and anxiety relate to the 'psyche'! Stress hormones can slow things down, so reassuring your patient is a big part of nursing care. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T004#GNS226_U3_T004_h2)

question: Which of these is a common everyday distraction during a home health visit?

options.A: Frequent interruptions from attending physicians
options.B: Mandatory shift-change meetings in the hallway
options.C: Strict hospital visiting hour regulations
options.D: Background noise from household sources and family members

explanation: Unlike quiet hospital wards, homes are full of life! TVs playing, pets barking, and family chatting can make focusing a bit tricky. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T3#GNS324_U2_T3_h2)

question: When should you collect a midstream urine sample for a lab culture if the patient needs antibiotics?

options.A: On the final day of the antibiotic course
options.B: Forty-eight hours after starting antibiotics
options.C: It does not matter when the sample is collected
options.D: Before giving the very first dose of antibiotic

explanation: Always collect the sample first! If you start antibiotics before taking the sample, the drug will kill the bacteria in the lab dish and give you a false negative result. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T2#GNS223_U8_T2_h8)

question: Why is it so important to check how a patient is feeling emotionally before teaching them about their medications?

options.A: Patients who are afraid will refuse to answer demographic survey questions
options.B: Fear and anxiety can prevent the patient from retaining instructions
options.C: Emotional distress changes the chemical makeup of oral medications
options.D: Anxious patients are more likely to experience drug allergies immediately

explanation: When someone is terrified or in pain, their brain is overloaded. Taking a moment to calm them down first helps them actually remember your teaching! [learn more](GNS215_U4_T6#GNS215_U4_T6_h1)

question: Which of these is a common interpersonal trigger for conflict among nurses on a unit?

options.A: Strict government healthcare regulations
options.B: The physical temperature of the nursing station
options.C: Poor communication and rushed handovers
options.D: The hospital's annual budget deficit

explanation: Rushed handovers and unclear messages easily lead to misunderstandings and hurt feelings between colleagues. Clear talk prevents unnecessary drama! [learn more](GST321_U5_T2#GST321_U5_T2_h3)

question: Which criterion is commonly used when setting priorities among several community health problems?

options.A: The color of the pamphlets printed by the health ministry
options.B: The personal preference of the visiting medical doctor
options.C: The distance from the capital city to the village
options.D: The seriousness and fatality rate of the condition

explanation: Problems that cause the most severe illness, disability, or death are usually placed at the top of the priority list. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h7)

question: You notice a red patch over a patient's lower back that does not turn white when you press it with your finger. What does this usually mean?

options.A: A normal reaction to sleeping on cotton sheets
options.B: An early stage pressure injury starting to form
options.C: A healing bruise from a previous minor fall
options.D: An allergic reaction to bath soap

explanation: Great catch! When skin stays red and doesn't blanch (turn white) under pressure, it's a key early warning sign that deep tissue is suffering from a lack of blood flow. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T10#GNS225_U5_T10_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a good trait for a rehabilitation goal?

options.A: It is kept completely vague so staff can change it anytime
options.B: It includes a specific deadline for completion
options.C: It focuses on clear, trackable outcomes
options.D: It is planned together with the patient

explanation: Good goals are never vague! They need to be specific and measurable so everyone knows what they are working toward. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T3#GNS123_U6_T3_h8)

question: What is the main goal of public health surveillance?

options.A: To continuously track health data and spot where diseases are hiding
options.B: To make cheap medicines for rural clinics
options.C: To diagnose patients with long-term mental illness
options.D: To punish hospitals that miss their cleaning schedules

explanation: Surveillance is like keeping a watchful eye on community health trends so we can catch outbreaks before they blow up. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T5#GNS313_U1_T5_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of the Incident Command System during a disaster?

options.A: To place financial responsibility solely on local nursing staff
options.B: To establish a clear chain of command and organized coordination
options.C: To allow every responder to make independent medical decisions
options.D: To eliminate the need for medical triage protocols

explanation: Well done! This system keeps everyone organized with clear leadership roles, stopping chaos and confusion when multiple agencies respond. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T3#GNS315_U1_T3_h5)

question: Why must nurses ask patients to remove all jewelry and hair pins before an MRI test?

options.A: Metal objects can fly into the magnet or cause severe burns
options.B: The hospital requires patients to keep valuables in a safe locker

question: Which hormones drive early heart and blood vessel changes in pregnancy?

options.A: Antidiuretic hormone
options.B: Estrogen and progesterone
options.C: Insulin and glucagon
options.D: Thyroid stimulating hormone

explanation: You've got this! High levels of estrogen and progesterone relax smooth muscles and help blood vessels grow to support the pregnancy. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T2#GNS121_U7_T2_h1)

question: When the inner lining of blood vessels gets damaged in preeclampsia, what is the main result?

options.A: Damaged kidney tissues heal rapidly
options.B: Blood vessels squeeze tight and leak fluid
options.C: Massive production of red blood cells
options.D: Uterine muscles permanently relax

explanation: Think of the blood vessels as having tiny leaks. When they get damaged, they tighten up and let fluid seep into body tissues, causing high BP and swelling. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T019#GNS226_U2_T019_h2)

question: What medical term is used to describe pain or a burning sensation when passing urine?

options.A: Nocturia
options.B: Dysuria
options.C: Proteinuria
options.D: Hematuria

explanation: Dysuria is the clinical term for painful or difficult urination, commonly reported during infections. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T2#GNS213_U4_T2_h2)

question: Why is it so helpful to involve local community leaders in public health campaigns?

options.A: It builds trust and encourages residents to adopt healthy behaviors.
options.B: It allows the government to avoid spending money on medical supplies.
options.C: It guarantees that no one in the village will ever catch a virus.
options.D: It removes the need for nurses to provide direct patient care.

explanation: You're right! Local leaders have the community's trust. When they support a health initiative, people are much more likely to listen and join in. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T76#GNS214_U1_T76_h7)

question: What is the main goal of giving psychological first aid to an abuse survivor?

options.A: Prescribing antidepressant medications to cure trauma permanently
options.B: Offering immediate comfort, safety, and supportive listening
options.C: Forcing the survivor to report the incident to the police
options.D: Conducting deep psychoanalysis of childhood experiences

explanation: Spot on! Psychological first aid is all about offering a comforting presence, meeting basic needs, and easing shock without pushing unwanted counseling. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T8#GNS312_U4_T8_h7)

question: In nursing, we say 'if it is not documented, it never happened.' What does this mean for patient education?

options.A: Patients completely forget everything the moment they leave the ward
options.B: Hospitals will not pay nurses for talking to patients
options.C: Doctors are the only staff allowed to speak about prescriptions
options.D: Verbal teaching has no legal proof without a written note in the chart

explanation: Documentation protects both you and the patient by providing legal proof that education actually took place. Always chart your care! [learn more](GNS215_U4_T7#GNS215_U4_T7_h2)

question: Why is checking the damage so important after a disaster occurs?

options.A: It allows the government to fine citizens who failed to evacuate
options.B: It replaces the need for search and rescue operations
options.C: It guarantees that no future disasters will ever occur in that zone
options.D: It helps agencies quantify losses and plan effective recovery efforts

explanation: Damage assessments give a clear picture of what was destroyed, helping authorities know how to send help and rebuild properly. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T9#GNS315_U1_T9_h4)

question: What are the three core parts of the epidemiological triangle?

options.A: Bacteria, virus, and fungi
options.B: Agent, host, and environment
options.C: Prevention, treatment, and cure
options.D: Patient, doctor, and nurse

explanation: Spot on! Think of it as a three-way puzzle: the germ (agent), the person (host), and their surroundings (environment). Keep building that foundation! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T77#GNS214_U1_T77_h2)

question: Which of these is a direct benefit of investing money into hospital technology?

options.A: Automatic curing of chronic non-communicable diseases
options.B: Zero operational costs for hospital management
options.C: Access to modern diagnostic tools like CT scanners
options.D: Elimination of the need for nursing documentation

explanation: Putting money into technology helps hospitals get modern machines, making it easier to find out what is wrong with a patient. [learn more](GST322_U3_T5#GST322_U3_T5_h3)
